text:
Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenshipU(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenshipT(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
Official(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
ManagerAtGazprom(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.
HoldCitizenship(x, y) ::: x holds citizenship y.
Vladimir ::: Vladimir.
Ekaterina ::: Ekaterina.
Premises:
∀x (CanRegister(x) → Participate(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the 2024 election.
CitizenshipU(x) → CanRegister(x) ::: If someone has U.S. citizenship, then they can register.
CitizenshipU(x) ∨ CitizenshipT(x) ::: A person either has U.S. or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldCitizenship(vladimir, Taiwanese) ::: No Russian Federation official holds Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldCitizenship(vladimir, ManagerAtGazprom) ::: Vladimir is not a manager at Gazprom.
HoldCitizenship(vladimir, Taiwanese) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(vladimir) ::: Vladimir either holds Taiwanese citizenship or is a manager at Gazprom.
CanRegister(Ekaterina) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(Ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register or is a manager at Gazprom.
Conclusion:
CanParticipate(Ekaterina) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(vladimir) ::: Ekaterina can participate in the 2024 election or Vladimir is a manager at Gazprom.
